title: First Launch Experience
description: The user opens Treehouse Living for the first time. They're guided through device detection, accent color selection, and an initial widget layout — arriving at a personalized dashboard within 60 seconds.
mermaid:
flowchart LR
    A([App Launch]) --> B[Boot Sequence & Device Scan]
    B --> C{Peripherals Found?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Show Detected Devices]
    C -- No --> E[No Devices State]
    D --> F[Accent Color Picker]
    E --> F
    F --> G{User Picks Color?}
    G -- Yes --> H[Apply Accent Color]
    G -- Skip --> I[Default to Cyan]
    H --> J[Widget Layout Selection]
    I --> J
    J --> K[/Performance/]
    J --> L[/Balanced/]
    J --> M[/Minimal/]
    K --> N[Populate Dashboard Grid]
    L --> N
    M --> N
    N --> O[Animate Widgets Into Position]
    O --> P[Show Completion Toast]
    P --> Q([Dashboard Ready])

steps.title: App opens — device scan begins
steps.description: The boot sequence animates while the system detects connected peripherals and hardware profile.

steps.title: Accent color picker appears
steps.description: User selects a system-wide accent color. Preview updates in real time behind the picker.
steps.branch: User can skip — defaults to cyan.

steps.title: Widget layout selection
steps.description: Three preset layouts are offered: Performance, Balanced, and Minimal. Selecting one populates the dashboard grid.

steps.title: Dashboard loads with chosen layout
steps.description: Widgets animate into position. A subtle toast confirms setup is complete. The user is on the dashboard and ready to explore.

engNotes: Boot sequence is driven by settings.js — sequence timing is configurable via token durations
Accent color persists to localStorage via settings-manager.js — key: treehouse-accent
Widget presets are defined in widgets.js — layout data is a JSON structure of grid positions
Edge case: if no peripherals detected, skip device scan and show a "no devices" state instead
